apps.ais_runner_tagline: Azure Integration Services — local development desktop
apps.ais_runner_description: Run and test Azure Logic Apps locally without pushing to Azure. One-click Azurite + func start, live run history, workflow analysis bar, Service Bus queue counts, CI/CD DevOps view, Liquid template tester, and workflow chain graph — all in one desktop app.
apps.ais_monitor_tagline: Azure Logic Apps workflow chain explorer
apps.ais_monitor_description: Visualise how your Logic Apps connect to each other via Service Bus queues and Event Grid, inspect live run history per chain, trigger HTTP workflows with saved payloads, and monitor deployed workflow states — all from a single desktop view.
apps.ais_tracing_tagline: Correlation-id tracer for Azure Cosmos DB
apps.ais_tracing_description: Follow a single value — a correlation id, an order reference — through every container of an Azure Cosmos DB account, and see where it got to. Samples your containers, works out which field links documents together, then draws each step on a timeline. Empty rows matter as much as full ones: they show where the data hasn't arrived.
apps.ais_analytics_tagline: Correlation-id tracer for Azure Log Analytics
apps.ais_analytics_description: The same tracer, aimed at a Log Analytics workspace instead of Cosmos DB. Paste a correlation id and see every step it touched — it works out which column ties the steps of one flow together straight from the data, then draws where that value got to and where it didn't. An empty lane is as meaningful as a full one.
apps.publishkit_tagline: AI-powered blog post manager with queue-to-publish workflow
apps.publishkit_description: Write, generate, and schedule blog posts from your desktop. AI drafting via Mistral or Claude, markdown editor with live preview, queue-to-publish flow, weekly auto-publish, and multi-language support (FR/EN) — all in one native app.
apps.shipscreen_tagline: The complete iOS & Android build and publish assistant
apps.shipscreen_description: Your perfect companion for shipping mobile apps. Build, run, and iterate locally on iOS and Android, then package release artifacts ready for the App Store and Google Play. Handles bundle IDs, signing config, version bumps, screenshot generation in every required size, and the device-frame marketing assets — all from a single native desktop app.
apps.spreadradar_tagline: Crypto price gaps across exchanges and Solana, live
apps.spreadradar_description: Follow any crypto asset on Binance, Bybit, OKX, MEXC, Gate and Jupiter at once. See the best cross-venue edges net of fees, which venue's price trails the others, and the tokens Gate or MEXC just listed that Binance does not have yet. Swap SOL/USDT on-chain through Jupiter from a local hot wallet, in a dry run at every start and within hard limits.
apps.polishcast_tagline: Record your screen, get a polished video: smooth cursor, zoom on clicks
apps.polishcast_description: Record from the menu bar or with a shortcut. The cursor is redrawn so it glides, clicks become zooms that ease in, and a background, padding and rounded corners frame the result. Adjust it in the editor, cut the pauses, and export to MP4 at up to 4K.
apps.jobscout_tagline: Job posts from LinkedIn and local boards, ranked against your profile
apps.jobscout_description: Collect job posts from LinkedIn and the main local boards of nine countries — Switzerland, Singapore, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates, Ireland, Belgium and Austria — into one list on your computer. Read each description in the app, score every job against your profile with Mistral or a local ollama model, and let saved searches run on their own and notify you about the good matches.
apps.surfacewatch_tagline: Watch a web app's client-side attack surface change between builds
apps.surfacewatch_description: Capture each target of a pentest engagement with REA and see its attack surface: endpoints, parameters, statuses, security headers and third parties. Compare two builds without the noise of renamed chunks and timing, turn what matters into findings backed by evidence, and retest to see whether each one is fixed. Runs fully local, with a command line for scheduled watches.
apps.gitagent_tagline: Agentic graph for commit and deploy workflows
apps.gitagent_description: Turns a dirty working tree into an open pull request, one approved step at a time. Scans your repo, drafts a commit message and a PR description with a local ollama model or Mistral, then commits, pushes, and opens the PR — but nothing touches git history or the remote without an explicit yes at each gated step.
apps.trackcut_tagline: Split long MP3/WAV recordings into tracks, from the keyboard
apps.trackcut_description: Load a live set, a radio show or a digitised tape and get one file per track. Silence detection proposes the splits, you confirm or nudge each one by ear, then export: MP3 without re-encoding, or MP3/FLAC/WAV with loudness normalisation and ReplayGain tags. Can also pull the audio of a YouTube link.

ais_runner.seo_title: AIS Runner — Run Azure Logic Apps Locally
ais_runner.seo_description: Desktop app for local Azure Logic Apps Standard development: one-click Azurite and Functions Core Tools, live run history, Liquid tests. No deploy.
overview: Developing Azure Logic Apps Standard normally means a slow loop: change a workflow, deploy it, trigger it, dig through the Azure portal to find out what happened, repeat. AIS Runner collapses that loop onto your own machine.

It starts the local stack for you — Azurite for storage emulation, Azure Functions Core Tools to host the workflow runtime — and then gives you the views the portal makes you hunt for: run history as it happens, how your workflows chain together, and what is sitting in your Service Bus queues.
It is a native desktop app written in Rust with Dioxus, so it starts instantly and stays out of the way of the rest of your toolchain.

features.title: Local stack from the toolbar
features.body: Azurite, the Service Bus Docker emulator, func start for Node.js workflows and mvn azure-functions:run for Java apps, each a button. func start runs pre-flight fixes first: package.json, connections.json ARM syntax, and stubs for missing settings.

features.title: Mock APIs
features.body: Scans every workflow.json, builds a contract of the outbound HTTP calls from adjacent Parse_JSON schemas, serves stubbed responses locally, and repoints the URL app settings at them. Stopping restores local.settings.json.

features.title: Record and replay tests
features.body: Capture a multi-step scenario — create a container, send a message, trigger a workflow — as plain JSON committed next to the workflows, then replay it with a live pass/fail per step, including waiting on a triggered run and asserting its outcome.

ais_tracing.seo_title: AIS Tracing — Correlation ID Tracer for Azure Cosmos DB
ais_tracing.seo_description: Follow a correlation ID or order reference through every container of an Azure Cosmos DB account and see exactly where it stopped.

AIS Tracing answers it in one step. It samples your containers, works out on its own which field links documents to each other, then follows your value across all of them and draws each step on a timeline.
The gaps are the point. A step with no document is not an empty result to scroll past — it is the answer, showing you exactly which hop the data never reached.

trackcut.seo_description: Split live sets, DJ mixes and long recordings into tracks from the keyboard: silence detection, gapless MP3 export without re-encoding, FLAC and WAV.

polishcast.seo_title: PolishCast — Screen Recorder, Smooth Cursor and Auto-Zoom
polishcast.seo_description: Screen recorder for macOS and Windows: redrawn smooth cursor, automatic zoom on clicks, rounded frame, pauses cut out, MP4 export up to 4K.
overview: A raw screen recording is hard to watch: the cursor jumps around, the text is tiny, and every pause where you were thinking is still in it.

PolishCast records the screen without the cursor and notes where the pointer goes. It then redraws a smooth cursor, zooms in where you clicked, and frames the video with a background, padding and rounded corners.
The editor lets you adjust each zoom, cut the silences and choose the frame. What you export is exactly what the preview shows.

features.title: Record from anywhere
features.body: Start and stop from the menu bar (macOS) or the notification area (Windows), or with ⌘⇧2 / Ctrl+Shift+2 from any app. The display your pointer is on is recorded with your microphone, and PolishCast's own windows are left out.

features.title: A cursor that glides
features.body: The cursor isn't recorded: it's redrawn from the pointer's path, so it moves smoothly, and it can be made bigger.

features.title: Zooms from your clicks
features.body: Each click becomes a zoom that eases in on where you clicked. On the timeline you change when it starts and ends, how deep it goes and where it looks, or add one at the playhead with Z.

features.title: Pauses cut out
features.body: Silences where nothing is said are left out, picture and sound together, with a moment kept around your words. Two sliders set what counts as a pause, and a click on the timeline puts one back.

features.title: A frame for every format
features.body: Screen, 16:9, 9:16 or square, with background, padding, corners, shadow, cursor size and smoothing. Every change can be undone and is saved as you go.

features.title: Light files, sharp export
features.body: MP4 at 1080p, 1440p or 4K, 30 or 60 fps, with your voice. On macOS each recording is shrunk to about a fifth of its size right after you stop, with no visible loss on text.

requirements: macOS 15 or later on Apple Silicon, or Windows 10 (version 2004) or later
Screen Recording and Microphone permissions, asked for on the first recording
An internet connection on first export, to download the video tool (ffmpeg) the app uses

faq.q: Is the Windows version ready?
faq.a: It is built and signed with every release, but it hasn't been run on a real Windows machine yet, so expect rough edges. macOS is the tested platform.

faq.q: Does it work on Linux?
faq.a: Not yet. Under Wayland, an app can't read where the pointer is in other apps, and the redrawn cursor depends on it.

faq.q: Where are my recordings?
faq.a: Each recording is a folder in Movies/PolishCast, with the video, the pointer movements and your edits. The exported MP4 is written next to it. Deleting a recording from the list moves it to the Trash, so you can still get it back.

faq.q: Do I need to install ffmpeg?
faq.a: No. The app downloads its own copy on first use and checks it against its published checksum. A copy already on your machine works too.

jobscout.seo_title: JobScout — LinkedIn and Local Job Boards, Scored for You
jobscout.seo_description: Collects job posts from LinkedIn and local boards in nine countries, from jobs.ch to StepStone, and scores each against your profile, on your machine.
overview: Looking for a job means the same search on three or four sites, the same post seen twice under different titles, and a browser full of tabs you meant to come back to. Deciding which posts are worth an application takes longer than finding them.

JobScout searches LinkedIn's public pages, without logging in, and the main local boards for one country at a time, in any of nine: Switzerland (jobs.ch, jobup.ch), Singapore (MyCareersFuture, JobStreet), Germany (Arbeitsagentur, StepStone), France (France Travail), the United Kingdom (Totaljobs, Reed), the United Arab Emirates (Bayt), Ireland (IrishJobs), Belgium and Austria (StepStone). Every job lands in one list on your computer, once, with a status you set: New, Saved, Applied or Hidden.

Each job can be scored against your profile by any OpenAI-compatible model, Mistral by default or ollama on your own machine. A score comes with a one-line verdict, the strengths and the gaps. Saved searches, called watches, run on their own while the app is open and notify you about new jobs above your threshold.

features.title: Several boards, one list
features.body: LinkedIn plus each country's own boards: jobs.ch and jobup.ch in Switzerland, StepStone and the Arbeitsagentur in Germany, Reed and Totaljobs in the UK, and more. A job posted on more than one site appears once.

features.title: No login, no account at risk
features.body: LinkedIn is read through its public guest pages, never with your account. All requests are paced, and a rate limit stops the run instead of retrying.

features.title: Scored against your profile
features.body: Mistral by default or a local ollama model gives each job a score, a one-line verdict, its strengths and its gaps. The API key is read from your environment and never written to disk.

features.title: Watches that notify you
features.body: Save a search and JobScout runs it every 1 to 72 hours while it is open, scores up to 15 new jobs and sends one desktop notification for those above your threshold — and, if you like, an email with the jobs and their links to your licence's address.

features.title: Yours, on your computer
features.body: Jobs, statuses, watches and your profile are kept in plain JSON files, one folder per country. Export the visible list to CSV at any time.

requirements: macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel), Windows 10 or 11 with the WebView2 Runtime, or Linux x86_64
An internet connection. No LinkedIn or job-board account is needed
For scoring: a Mistral API key or another OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or ollama running locally
For JobStreet on Windows and Linux: Python with Camoufox (pip install -U camoufox && python -m camoufox fetch)

faq.q: Does JobScout use my LinkedIn account?
faq.a: No. It reads LinkedIn's public guest pages, the ones anyone sees without logging in, so your account is never involved and never at risk.

faq.q: Where are the jobs kept?
faq.a: On your computer, in JobScout's data folder, with one folder per country. Nothing is sent anywhere except the searches themselves and, if you score jobs, the job and your profile to the model you chose. With ollama, that stays on your machine too.

faq.q: Which countries are supported?
faq.a: Nine, on every plan: Switzerland (jobs.ch, jobup.ch), Singapore (MyCareersFuture, JobStreet), Germany (Arbeitsagentur, StepStone), France (France Travail), the United Kingdom (Totaljobs, Reed), the United Arab Emirates (Bayt), Ireland (IrishJobs), Belgium and Austria (StepStone), each with LinkedIn too. surfacewatch.seo_title: SurfaceWatch — Client-Side Attack Surface for Web Pentests
surfacewatch.seo_description: Desktop app and CLI that maps a web app's client-side attack surface with REA and shows what changed between builds, with evidence. Fully local.
overview: A web app under test changes every sprint. Comparing two builds by hand means wading through renamed script chunks, images and timing differences to find the one new endpoint that matters, and remembering which findings were fixed since the last visit.

SurfaceWatch captures each target of an engagement with REA and turns the traffic into a surface: every endpoint with its parameters and statuses, the security headers, the scripts and the third parties the page talks to. Entries worth a look, such as server errors, admin paths that answer without a login or pages without a Content-Security-Policy, are flagged first.

Compare any two captures and see only what changed, each change with what it means for your testing. Findings cite the raw REA evidence they rest on, and a retest says whether each one is fixed. Everything runs on your computer and no LLM is involved.

features.title: The surface, not the traffic
features.body: Endpoints with their parameters, statuses and security headers, plus scripts and third-party origins. Suspicious entries are flagged and listed first.

features.title: Diffs without the noise
features.body: Renamed chunks, images and timing never show up as changes. A stability check captures the build twice and sets aside endpoints that come and go between runs.

features.title: Findings with evidence
features.body: Promote any entry or change to a finding. Each one cites the REA evidence it rests on, and a retest records whether it is fixed.

features.title: Engagements that stay in scope
features.body: Each engagement records the client, who authorised the test and its test window. Captures outside the window are refused, and origins are checked as you type.

features.title: Desktop and command line
features.body: The surfacewatch-cli command line shares the same core, for scheduled watches from cron or CI, HAR imports and checks over SSH.

requirements: macOS (Apple Silicon), Windows 10 or 11, or Linux x86_64
REA: a global rea if installed, otherwise it is run through npx
Google Chrome, Chromium or Edge
Written authorisation for every target you capture

faq.q: What is REA?
faq.a: REA is the open-source tool SurfaceWatch drives to open each target in a browser and record what it does. SurfaceWatch keeps REA's raw evidence unchanged and builds the surface and the diffs on top of it.

faq.q: Does anything leave my computer?
faq.a: No. Captures, surfaces, findings and engagements are kept in private files on your computer. SurfaceWatch talks only to the targets you capture, and no AI model is involved.

faq.q: Can I capture any website?
faq.a: Only targets you are authorised to test. Every engagement needs an authorisation note and a test window, and captures outside that window are refused.
